To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the BipoSH representation of SI-violation is a powerful tool that can be used to identify and characterize NC-beam effects in CMB maps and (ii) the BipoSh representation of SI-violations in the WMAP-7 data is consistent with the expected NC-beam effects.

(1) CMB maps of signal that respects SI symmetry, measured with a mildly non-circular beam, will exhibit apparent SI violation and (2) BipoSH measures constructed from such CMB maps can reveal this apparent SI violation.

(1) the Bipolar Spherical Harmonic (BipoSH)-based measure, $\mathcal{S}_{00}$, of SI violation is sensitive to the NC-beam effect and (2) the NC-beam induced SI violation can be mitigated by applying the appropriate correction to the BipoSH-based SI measures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of the non-circularity of the instrument beam on the statistical isotropy of the CMB maps.
developing and implementing a novel method of measuring the statistical isotropy (or anisotropy) of the Cosmic Microwave Background ( CMB ) radiation.
developing a framework that can be used to assess the impact of NC-beam effects on SI measures in CMB experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NC beam effects, while unavoidable, are a significant source of SI violation and must be taken into account in the analysis of CMB maps.
the WMAP 7-year maps are consistent with the standard model of cosmology and that there is no evidence of SI violation.
the WMAP-7 maps do not show any significant violation of SI, and that NC-beam effect is the most likely cause of the observed mild deviations from SI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BipoSH measures can be used to detect NC-beam effects in CMB data.
the NC beam of WMAP-7 instrument, coupled with the scan-strategy of the instrument is sufficient to explain the observed SI violation in WMAP- 7 maps.

the BipoSH measures are capable of capturing subtle NC-beam effect in CMB maps and that the NC-beam effects in the CMB maps are unavoidable, even when the underlying SI is respected by the cosmological signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to instrumental noise and astrophysical contaminants, NC-beam effects are a new and unavoidable source of SI violation in current CMB experiments.
the NC-beam effect is not a mere nuisance that can be ignored.
, while the NC-beam effects are unavoidable in current experiments, they can be mitigated by using appropriate SI violation measures.
